items.title: Patient's self-monitoring of urate during allopurinol titration in primary care: a feasibility study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of patient-led self-monitoring of plasma urate and dose escalation of allopurinol, in primary care, from the perspectives of patients and healthcare personnel. Management of patients with gout remains suboptimal, improvement can involve a self-monitoring procedure. There are no prior studies testing the feasibility of self-monitoring of urate during titration of allopurinol supported by nurses in primary care. A mixed-methods study. Interviews with general practitioners and patients in Swedish primary care. Quantitative data was collected from patients using quality of life and person-centeredness questionnaires, and from personnel about perceived acceptability, relevance and feasibility of the procedure tested. Electronic health records were reviewed. The measure-report-titrate procedure and its introduction was considered acceptable, appropriate and feasible by all participants. Challenges identified included practical difficulties in using the urate meter and limited confidence in the accuracy of the urate measures. All patients completed the procedure and achieved their target urate level. Personnel persisted requiring necessary conditions for a successful implementation. Patients and personnel reported increased awareness and knowledge, ease of anxiety about disease progression and an experience of receiving individualized care. Self-monitoring of urate during allopurinol titration may serve as an alternative to regular laboratory testing. The measure-report-titrate procedure appeared to enhance patients' knowledge of treatment and increase engagement in their care. These findings will inform the implementation of nurse-led gout management in primary care.

items.title: Serum microRNA Landscape in Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Hypothesis-Generating Reference Dataset.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an eosinophilic vasculitis arising against a background of adult-onset asthma. We investigated circulating microRNA (miRNA) profiles in EGPA and integrated them with previously reported serum protein data. In this retrospective, cross-sectional study, archived sera from 14 patients with active, glucocorticoid-naïve EGPA and 20 with severe eosinophilic asthma without EGPA were profiled on a 2,588-miRNA microarray. Differential expression among 1,777 quantifiable miRNAs was assessed with limma, adjusting for sex and RNA integrity number; significance required both a Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate below 0.05 and a Bonferroni-corrected p below 0.05. TargetScan-predicted target genes were intersected with 29 serum proteins previously shown to differ between the same groups. Two further paired analyses, each performed in a separate group of patients with EGPA, compared active disease with the glucocorticoid-treated phase (n = 11) and samples before versus after mepolizumab (n = 13). Eight miRNAs met both criteria: hsa-miR-3126-5p, hsa-miR-921, hsa-miR-6836-5p and hsa-miR-668-5p were lower in EGPA, and hsa-miR-6857-3p, hsa-miR-1260a, hsa-miR-603 and hsa-miR-12125 were higher (within-cohort areas under the curve, 0.82-0.94). Fourteen of the 29 proteins were encoded by predicted target genes. Only hsa-miR-3678-3p changed after glucocorticoid treatment; no miRNA changed after mepolizumab, and none of the eight EGPA-associated miRNAs changed with either treatment. This exploratory study identifies circulating miRNA differences between EGPA and severe eosinophilic asthma, and the complete result table is provided as a reference resource. Independent validation is required to establish their biological and clinical significance. UMIN000040163.

items.title: Soil-transmitted helminths modulate immune responses and attenuate disease activity in treatment-naive rheumatoid arthritis patients.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by systemic inflammation and progressive joint damage. Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infection may modulate host immunity, but its role in RA pathogenesis remains unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 173 treatment-naïve RA patients and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Disease activity was assessed using DAS28-CRP and CDAI. Immune profiling, including ELISA, flow cytometry, and multiplex cytokine analysis, was performed. STH-positive RA patients exhibited reduced disease activity and lower acute-phase proteins. Immune dysregulation observed in helminth-negative RA was partially normalized in STH-positive individuals, with broad suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. IL-6, MCP-1, and IP-10 discriminated between groups (AUC > 0.75). Helminth infection independently predicted lower IL-6, TNF-α, and MCP-1. Key pathways included cytokine-receptor interactions, JAK-STAT signalling, and TNF signalling. STH infection is associated with attenuated inflammation and immune modulation in RA, suggesting a potential role for helminth-driven immunoregulation in disease pathogenesis and therapy.

items.title: Familial Mediterranean fever across the age spectrum: pediatric and adult-onset differences in phenotype, diagnosis, treatment response, and outcomes.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an auto-inflammatory disease caused by pathogenic variants in the MEFV gene, leading to dysregulated pyrin inflammasome activation and excessive IL-1β-mediated inflammation. FMF is characterized by recurrent fever, serositis, and musculoskeletal manifestations, with substantial interindividual variability. Although traditionally considered a pediatric disease, FMF is now recognized as a lifelong condition extending into adulthood, with age-related differences in clinical presentation, genetics, treatment response, and long-term outcomes. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence comparing pediatric-onset disease, adult-onset FMF, and adults with childhood-onset disease across these domains. A structured narrative search of current evidence on FMF was conducted using different platforms, highlighting differences in clinical presentation, genotype-phenotype correlations, treatment response, and quality of life. Research indicates that pediatric-onset FMF is typically associated with earlier and more severe disease, higher attack frequency, and a stronger association with high-penetrance pathogenic variants, particularly M694V. In contrast, adult-onset FMF patients often exhibit milder and atypical manifestations, lower inflammatory burden, and a higher prevalence of heterozygous or low-penetrance variants, although diagnostic delays remain common in this population. Adults with childhood-onset FMF represent a distinct subgroup with cumulative inflammatory exposure and a higher risk of complications, including AA amyloidosis. Across all age groups, colchicine remains the cornerstone of therapy, although treatment challenges differ, with higher rates of colchicine resistance in children and greater intolerance and comorbidity-related constraints in adults. Recognizing FMF as a disease continuum may enhance clinical awareness, facilitate earlier diagnosis, and support age-adapted, proactive management strategies aimed at reducing long-term complications and preserving quality of life. • FMF is clinically and genetically heterogeneous, with established differences between pediatric- and adult-onset disease. Delayed diagnosis and persistent inflammation contribute to preventable disease burden and complications. • This review directly compares pediatric-onset, adult-onset, and adult with childhood-onset FMF across multiple domains. This distinction highlights how age at onset and cumulative inflammatory exposure may lead to different disease trajectories in adulthood, linking phenotype, diagnostic recognition, genotype, treatment timing, and long-term outcomes within an age-continuum framework.

items.title: Acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis: a case report.
items.abstract: Although thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is occasionally observed in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc), thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is extremely rare. Herein, we report a rare case of limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc) complicated by TTP. A 44-year-old woman with anti-centromere antibody (ACA)-positive lcSSc of two years' duration presented with purpura, severe thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia. Her blood pressure, serum creatinine levels, and neurological examination results were normal. Although TTP, SSc-associated TMA, and scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) were considered in the differential diagnosis, plasma exchange alone was initially started because glucocorticoids (GCs) are associated with an increased risk of renal crisis. Subsequent testing revealed ADAMTS13 activity below 1%, with an inhibitor level of 1.0 Bethesda units (BU)/mL, establishing a diagnosis of acquired TTP. Despite starting prednisolone 40 mg/day, her platelet count dropped to 8,000/μL and she developed dysarthria, right hemiparesis, fever, and facial palsy. Moreover, her inhibitor level rose to 1.9 BU/mL after eight exchanges. GC pulse therapy and rituximab were added while plasma exchange continued. The platelet count recovered, and she has remained relapse-free for four years. A literature review identified 16 reports on 17 patients with SSc and TTP. None met current diagnostic criteria or had a documented ACA. In conclusion, acquired TTP can occur in ACA-positive lcSSc. Empirical GC therapy while awaiting the ADAMTS13 result may be considered in selected patients in whom TTP is strongly suspected and the estimated risk of SRC is low.

items.title: Tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement of ANCA-associated vasculitis: A diagnostic challenge mimicking infective endocarditis.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) are small-vessel vasculitides with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Cardiac valvular involvement is rare and may closely mimic infective endocarditis, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Tricuspid valve involvement, especially at the subvalvular apparatus, is particularly uncommon. We report a case of a 46-year-old man who presented with constitutional symptoms, pulmonary nodules with cavitation, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and positive c-ANCA with anti-proteinase-3 antibodies. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a serpiginous vegetation attached to the tricuspid subvalvular apparatus, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, extensive infectious evaluation, including multiple blood cultures, was negative. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune crescentic and necrotizing glomerulonephritis, supporting a diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Antibiotics were discontinued, and the patient was treated with glucocorticoids, rituximab, and avacopan, resulting in marked clinical improvement. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the subvalvular apparatus vegetation without surgical intervention. This case highlights a rare presentation of GPA with tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement and underscores the importance of distinguishing AAV-related endocardial disease from infective endocarditis. Histopathologic findings, particularly renal biopsy, can be critical in establishing the correct diagnosis. Recognition of this entity is essential, as appropriate immunosuppressive therapy may lead to resolution of valvular lesions and avoidance of unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or surgical intervention.

items.title: Recurrence of eosinophilic pneumonia after switching from mepolizumab to tezepelumab for worsening asthma in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: A 50-year-old woman with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis had maintained glucocorticoid-free remission for approximately four years with mepolizumab monotherapy. Because asthma control gradually deteriorated despite sustained control of systemic disease, mepolizumab was replaced with tezepelumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin. Asthma symptoms improved rapidly, and fractional exhaled nitric oxide levels decreased. However, peripheral blood eosinophil counts progressively increased, and computed tomography approximately six months after the switch demonstrated recurrent eosinophilic pneumonia, with pulmonary consolidations closely resembling those at the initial presentation. Prednisolone and mepolizumab were reintroduced, resulting in rapid resolution of eosinophilia and pulmonary infiltrates. Glucocorticoids were subsequently discontinued again without recurrence. This case suggests that improvement in airway symptoms after biologic switching does not necessarily indicate adequate suppression of systemic eosinophilic inflammation. Even after prolonged glucocorticoid-free remission, replacement of interleukin-5-targeted therapy with thymic stromal lymphopoietin inhibition may permit recurrence of eosinophilic disease. Peripheral blood eosinophil counts and systemic manifestations should therefore be carefully monitored after such switching in patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

items.title: Primary Sjögren's Syndrome Presenting With Complete Atrioventricular Block and Myocardial Injury: A Rare Immune-Mediated Cardiac Case Report.
items.abstract: Primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is a systemic autoimmune disorder predominantly involving exocrine glands; cardiac complications represent rare extra-glandular manifestations, and complete atrioventricular block (CAVB) is uncommon. We report a 58-year-old female presenting with acute chest tightness and transient loss of consciousness. Her electrocardiogram showed CAVB with ventricular escape rhythm and elevated cardiac troponin-I. Emergency coronary angiography excluded significant obstructive coronary artery disease. Positive anti-SSA, anti-SSB, anti-Ro52, cardiac-specific autoantibodies, together with minor salivary gland biopsy, confirmed pSS. She received methylprednisolone and hydroxychloroquine for immunomodulation, plus dual-chamber permanent pacemaker implantation for persistent symptomatic conduction defects. Symptoms resolved and cardiac biomarkers normalized in short-term follow-up. This case alerts clinicians to pSS-related immune-mediated cardiac injury as a differential diagnosis for unexplained CAVB after excluding coronary artery disease.

items.title: Double struggle: The influence of premenstrual symptoms on quality of life in women with Ankylosing Spondylitis - A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic autoimmune disease that often affects women of reproductive age, making the evaluation of premenstrual symptoms (PMS) important. The authors conducted a descriptive and correlational study including 84 women with AS in Turkey. PMS was measured using the Premenstrual Symptom Scale, while quality of life was assessed with the Ankylosing Spondylitis Quality of Life Scale. The authors found that PMS decreased with increasing age and disease duration. Through regression analysis, the authors found that higher PMS scores, older age, and older age at menarche were associated with poorer quality of life. The authors emphasize that reducing PMS may improve quality of life in women with AS.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Digital Patient Education in Rheumatoid Arthritis: An economic evaluation from a randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Self-management support is essential in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The WebRA trial showed that digital patient education (PE) improves self-efficacy, supports self-management, and reduces outpatient visits. This study assessed the 12-month cost-effectiveness from a partial societal perspective. Adults newly diagnosed with RA were randomised to digital or face-to-face PE. Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were estimated from EQ-5D-5L measurements over 12 months. Costs were obtained from national registries and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated. The probability of cost-effectiveness was estimated using probabilistic sensitivity analysis. Minimal important change in self-efficacy was the secondary outcome. Baseline characteristics of the 175 participants were balanced (intervention vs control): 60.7% vs 61.5% female, mean age 58 vs 56 years, and mean disease activity score (DAS28) 4.4 vs 4.6. Digital PE led to lower healthcare costs (€9,322 vs €9,886), and minor QALY gains (mean difference 0.013). The intervention was dominant in both adjusted and crude models, with ICERs of -€43,692/QALY and -€24,056/QALY, respectively. In bootstrap analyses, 47.3% (adjusted) and 52.7% (crude) of iterations fell in the south-east quadrant (lower costs, better outcomes). Probability of cost-effectiveness reached 71.5% at a €22,665/QALY threshold. For self-efficacy, digital PE was cost-saving, but effects were small and inconsistent. Digital PE was associated with lower costs and a small QALY gain compared with face-to-face PE, with a moderate probability of cost-effectiveness. Digital PE may be a cost-effective alternative; however, the estimated effects were subject to some uncertainty and sensitivity to model specification. Further investigation in broader populations is warranted.

items.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Immunogenicity of Biosimilar versus Reference Adalimumab in Methotrexate-Refractory Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Phase III Comparative Study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by dysregulated immune responses, persistent synovial inflammation, and involvement of multiple pro-inflammatory mediators, leading to progressive joint damage. Although adalimumab has substantially improved RA management, high-cost limits patient access. Biosimilars offer accessibility, while maintaining comparable efficacy and safety. To compare efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD) and immunogenicity of test adalimumab (Oriadali ® ) a proposed adalimumab biosimilar, with reference adalimumab (Humira ® ) in Indian patients with active RA inadequately controlled by methotrexate (MTX). In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled Phase III study, 201 patients with active RA were randomized (2:1) to receive test adalimumab (n=134) or reference adalimumab (n=67). The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response at Week 24, assessed using a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 28%. Secondary endpoints included ACR 20 response at Week 12, ACR50/70 at Week 24, Disease Activity Score based on 28 joints (DAS-28), C-reactive protein (CRP), Health Assessment Questionnaire-Disability Index (HAQ-DI), PK, PD, safety, and immunogenicity using anti-drug antibody (ADA) assessment. ACR 20 responses at Week 24 were achieved by 120/121 (99.2%) patients receiving test adalimumab and 63/63 (100.0%) patients receiving reference adalimumab (difference of -0.01 95% CI: -0.03 to 0.02; p=0.4693), demonstrating non-inferiority. At Week 12, ACR20 responses were achieved by 90.1% and 92.1% of patients in both groups, respectively. At Week 24, ACR50 responses were 61.2% versus 57.1%, and ACR70 responses were 32.3% versus 33.3%. DAS28, CRP and HAQ-DI improved similarly in both groups. PK exposure was comparable, with all parameters within bioequivalence limits (T/R ratio of Cmax 100.16%; AUC 0 -t 102.99%), Changes in IL-6, TNF- α and immunogenicity were comparable between groups. Most Adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate, with no serious adverse events reported. Test adalimumab biosimilar demonstrated comparable efficacy, safety PK, PD, and immunogenicity profiles to reference adalimumab, supporting its use in patients with active RA receiving methotrexate. items.title: Immunometabolic Reprogramming in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Mechanistic Evidence, Candidate Biomarkers, and Translational Challenges.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease in which inflammatory signaling and cellular metabolism interact within the synovial microenvironment. This narrative review critically examines glucose, lipid and amino-acid metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and their cell-specific roles in synovial fibroblasts, macrophages, lymphocytes and other joint-resident or infiltrating cells. Human tissue and observational metabolomic studies support the presence of metabolic alterations in RA, whereas causal mechanisms are established predominantly through experimental perturbation in cell-based and animal models. Lactate, lipid signatures, kynurenine-pathway metabolites and oxidative-stress measures are promising candidate biomarkers, but none of the metabolic endotypes discussed here is established as a clinically validated tool for treatment selection. Methotrexate and approved disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs remain the clinical standard; direct glycolytic or glutaminolytic inhibitors, repurposed metabolic modulators, traditional Chinese medicine interventions, stimulus-responsive carriers, and nucleic-acid or gene-based approaches require substantially more RA-specific clinical validation. We synthesize the evidence by model and translational maturity, highlight conflicting or context-dependent observations, and identify key barriers including cohort heterogeneity, assay standardization, off-target toxicity and prospective validation. The resulting framework positions immunometabolism as a testable contribution to RA biology rather than an established precision-treatment algorithm.

items.title: Knowledge Mapping and Research Hotspots of Comorbidities in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Past 20 Years.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease, whose health impact extends beyond itself and its treatment, and is also associated with various comorbidities. Early identification of comorbidities and development of personalized treatment plans are associated with improved clinical outcomes. This study aims to summarize the knowledge structure in the field of SLE comorbidities and further explore its research hotspots and trends through bibliometrics. A search was conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed for literature on comorbidities of SLE from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used for collaborative network analysis, co-citation analysis of references, and keyword co-occurrence analysis on these publications. The analysis included 2140 records, with the United States leading in publication volume. Major contributing institutions included Harvard University, Harvard University Medical Affiliates, and the University of London, and the most productive authors were Chiara Tani and Eloisa Bonfa. The most cited reference was Anders HJ (2020) with 724 citations. Key themes identified by keyword co-occurrence analysis included autoimmune comorbidities, cardiovascular risk, clinical management, patient-reported outcomes, and methodological innovations. Co-citation analysis suggested a shift from an earlier focus on classical comorbidities to reproductive health and COVID-19, and a more recent shift to global epidemiology, updated treatment guidelines, and cardiovascular risk management. This bibliometric analysis provides a comprehensive overview of research on SLE comorbidities over the past 20 years, highlighting the growth trend, collaborative mechanisms, research priorities, and progress in clinical trials in this field, while emphasizing emerging hot topics such as autoimmune diseases and atherosclerosis. These findings reflect patterns and thematic concerns of research activity rather than direct measures of research quality or clinical importance. Future research may benefit from increased international collaboration and further exploration of emerging comorbidities.

items.title: Nonlinear U-shaped association between serum uric acid and erythrocyte sedimentation rate in ankylosing spondylitis: a sex-stratified analysis of turning points.
items.abstract: Previous studies on the UA-inflammation relationship in ankylosing spondylitis have predominantly utilized traditional regression models assuming monotonic associations, masking non-linearities and sex-specific heterogeneity. This study aimed to characterize the sex-specific non-linear dose-response relationship between serum UA and ESR and to explore potential sex-specific turning points. This retrospective study included 1,182 hospitalized AS patients. RCS models were employed to assess non-linear associations, with robustness validated via Bootstrap resampling. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent determinants of hyperuricemia; four progressively adjusted sensitivity models confirmed association stability; and sex-stratified analyses evaluated sex-specific heterogeneity. The overall cohort demonstrated a significant U-shaped UA-ESR association ( P for nonlinearity<0.001), with the fully adjusted turning point at 375 μmol/L (Bootstrap 95% CI: 365-386); the nonlinear model outperformed the linear specification (R 2  = 0.097 vs. 0.043). The turning point remained stable across all sensitivity models (375-390 μmol/L). Marked sex differences were confirmed ( P for interaction<0.001): males showed a robust U-shaped association (turning point: 371 μmol/L; R 2  = 0.081 vs. 0.021 for linear), whereas females showed a persistent linear negative correlation without a reproducible turning point ( P for nonlinearity=0.376). The U-shaped pattern was not replicated with CRP, which showed a purely linear inverse association ( P for nonlinearity=0.248), indicating that the rebound is ESR-specific. This study demonstrates sex-specific nonlinear UA-ESR associations in AS, with a statistical turning point at approximately 371 μmol/L in males but no comparable turning point in females. These findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for sex-stratified UA management in AS, pending prospective validation.

items.title: Imaging therapeutic response at brain neuroimmune interfaces in women with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) frequently affects the central nervous system, likely via neuroimmune interfaces; how these interfaces respond longitudinally to standard therapy remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify these therapeutic dynamics. This retrospective longitudinal study included 63 women with SLE who had brain MRI at baseline and after standard therapy. Enlarged perivascular spaces (ePVS), choroid plexus (CP), and gray matter (GM) volumes were segmented from 3D T1-weighted images; the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was computed from DTI scans. Paired t-tests compared baseline and post-therapy values. Patients were grouped into neuropsychiatric SLE (NPSLE) and non-NPSLE groups, and longitudinal deltas compared. Spearman correlations assessed associations of MRI changes with clinical measures. After standard therapy, all 63 patients showed clinical improvement (decreased SLEDAI-2K, increased MoCA scores). Left DTI-ALPS index increased (T = -2.475, P FDR = 0.048), and bilateral CP volumes decreased (left: T = 2.432, P FDR = 0.048; right: T = 3.330, P FDR = 0.006). ePVS volumes remained unchanged. No significant correlations emerged between MRI changes and clinical scores, and improvement did not differ between NPSLE and non-NPSLE subgroups. Longitudinal MRI identified measurable alterations in Neuroimmune Interfaces in women with SLE, particularly the DTI-ALPS index and CP volume. These changes correlate with clinical improvement and serve as supplementary imaging biomarkers for assessing disease activity, independent of neuropsychiatric involvement.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of golimumab in ankylosing spondylitis and axial spondyloarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: Golimumab is an approved tumor necrosis factor inhibitor for the treatment of ankylosing spondylitis (AS) and axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Although randomized controlled trials have demonstrated its efficacy, evidence regarding long-term treatment maintenance remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy, safety, and durability of golimumab therapy in patients with AS and axSpA. This review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251130466). PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to January 2026. Randomized placebo-controlled trials of subcutaneous or intravenous golimumab were pooled using random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with Hartung-Knapp 95% confidence intervals (CIs), analyzing the approved dose in multi-arm trials; extension studies were synthesized separately as single-arm proportions. Primary outcomes were ASAS20, ASAS40, BASDAI50, and serious adverse events (SAEs). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (trials) and the NHLBI before-after tool (extensions), and certainty with GRADE. Seven publications representing four independent trials (834 randomized patients) were included. At Weeks 14-16, golimumab increased ASAS20 (RR 2.22, 95% CI 1.51-3.27; high certainty), ASAS40 (RR 3.25, 95% CI 1.89-5.59; high certainty), and BASDAI50 responses (RR 2.82, 95% CI 1.39-5.71; moderate certainty), corresponding to approximately 300-350 additional responders per 1,000 patients treated. Effects favored golimumab in both radiographic AS and non-radiographic axSpA, with no statistically significant subgroup difference (ASAS20, p  = 0.065). Evidence on SAEs was very imprecise (three trials, 14 events; RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.08-8.54; low certainty), and the risk of any adverse event was similar to placebo (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.85-1.29). In uncontrolled extensions, 72% (95% CI 35%-92%) and 63% (95% CI 31%-86%) of patients originally randomized to golimumab had ASAS20 and ASAS40 responses at Weeks 52-104 (very low certainty). High- to moderate-certainty randomized evidence shows that golimumab substantially improves short-term signs and symptoms of AS and axSpA compared with placebo. Safety data are too sparse to exclude important differences in serious adverse events, and evidence on durability of response is of very low certainty. All included trials were industry-sponsored, and independent long-term comparative studies are needed. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251130466, PROSPERO CRD420251130466.

items.title: Effects of cognitive behavioral therapy on psychological and physical outcomes in adults with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: Pain and functional limitations associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can substantially impair patients' psychological and physical well-being. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may alleviate psychological and physical symptoms in patients with RA by modifying maladaptive cognitions and behaviors and promoting adaptive coping with the disease. However, the effect of CBT in RA patients has not been systematically established. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from database inception to July 9, 2026, for relevant studies. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were independently performed by two reviewers. Any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or adjudicated by a third reviewer. Meta-analyses were primarily implemented through random-effects models. Effect estimates were presented as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twelve RCTs involving 1,538 participants with RA were incorporated. CBT was associated with lower levels of depression (SMD = -0.35, 95% CI: -0.55 to -0.14, low-certainty evidence), anxiety (SMD = -0.20, 95% CI: -0.32 to -0.08, moderate-certainty evidence), and fatigue (SMD = -0.44, 95% CI: -0.66 to -0.22, low-certainty evidence). At the 6-month follow-up, the pooled SMDs were -0.42 (95% CI, -0.63 to -0.20) for depression and -0.22 (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.01) for anxiety, based on six RCTs with available follow-up data. For sleep, the pooled estimate favored CBT, although this finding was based on only two studies and was supported by very-low-certainty evidence. No statistically significant between-group differences were noted for pain, physical function, or quality-of-life (QoL). Substantial heterogeneity was observed for depression and fatigue, and the 95% prediction intervals crossed the line of no effect for both outcomes. Exploratory subgroup analyses by CBT delivery format revealed no significant differences between subgroups. The pooled estimates suggested that CBT may be associated with lower levels of fatigue, anxiety, and depression in patients with RA. However, substantial heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing the line of no effect, and low certainty of evidence limit the reliability of these outcomes. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261470674, CRD420261470674.

items.title: Granzyme K associates with inflammatory immune programs and B-cell dysregulation in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterized by systemic immune activation and multi-organ inflammation. Granzyme K (GZMK), a serine protease predominantly expressed by CD8 + T cells and natural killer cells, has emerging non-cytotoxic inflammatory functions, but its relevance to SLE remains incompletely defined. In this study, we conducted investigations using plasma and tissue analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, an animal model, and primary human B cell experiments. Plasma GZMK was increased in patients with SLE and was associated with clinical disease activity. Integrated multi-tissue single cell analysis identified preferential GZMK enrichment in CD8 + effector memory T (Tem) cells and a higher relative abundance of this compartment in SLE, while proteomic profiling and multiplex immunofluorescence provided protein and tissue level evidence for a GZMK-enriched CD8 + memory T cell population. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested enhanced predicted communication between Tem and B lineage cells, and circulating GZMK was further associated with a plasma cell-like population. In two murine models, PPACK, which can inhibit GZMK catalytic activity but is not GZMK selective, attenuated lupus associated inflammatory phenotypes and partially normalized altered splenic B cell composition. In vitro experiments showed that active recombinant GZMK augmented plasma-cell-associated phenotypic and transcriptional responses under B cell expansion conditions. Collectively, these findings identify circulating GZMK as an independent correlate of SLE clinical activity and characterize a recurrent GZMK-enriched CD8 + memory/Tem cell program across peripheral blood and affected tissues that is associated with B-cell dysregulation and plasma-cell-related immune abnormalities.

items.title: Severe Calcific Aortic Stenosis in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Severe calcific aortic stenosis (CAS) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is exceptionally rare. SLE affects multiple organ systems, including the cardiovascular system. Cardiovascular mortality in SLE is approximately three times higher than in the general population, and cardiovascular morbidity affects about 25% of patients. Although valvular heart disease (VHD) is common in SLE, marked aortic stenosis, particularly severe CAS, remains uncommon. This case report describes a 60-year-old female patient with SLE and VHD who developed rapid progressive, severe, symptomatic CAS. A multidisciplinary heart team determined that she was at prohibitive risk for surgical aortic valve replacement, and she subsequently underwent high-risk transcatheter aortic valve implantation. No SLE flare occurred. Regular cardiovascular risk assessment and echocardiographic screening are essential for patients with SLE. Careful multidisciplinary and immunosuppressive management supports successful interventions while minimizing the risk of SLE flare.

items.title: Prevalence of Axial and Peripheral Musculoskeletal Manifestations and Comorbidities in Adult Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis in Qassim, Saudi Arabia.
items.abstract: This study aimed to describe the demographic, clinical, and therapeutic characteristics of adult patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) in Qassim, Saudi Arabia, and to identify independent predictors of axial and peripheral arthritis. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 185 adult patients with PsA attending rheumatology and dermatology clinics were reviewed. Associations between axial or peripheral arthritis and demographic, clinical, and comorbidity variables were assessed using chi-square(χ²)/Fisher's exact tests and the Mann-Whitney Z-test, followed by multivariate logistic regression adjusted for age at diagnosis, BMI, and vitamin D deficiency. The cohort was young (mean age 39.2±14.5 years) with balanced gender distribution (96, 51.9% male) and early onset PsA (96, 51.9% diagnosed before age 30). Skin-related symptoms were the most frequent presentation (122, 65.9%). Axial arthritis was uncommon (18, 9.7%); peripheral arthritis affected 60 patients (32.4%). Vitamin D deficiency was highly prevalent (124, 67.0%). Systemic therapy was given to 132 patients (71.4%), most frequently methotrexate (38, 20.5%). Axial arthritis was independently predicted by presenting symptoms (adjusted odds ratio (AOR)=0.189, 95% CI 0.056-0.644, p=0.008 for skin-related vs arthritis-dominant presentation). Peripheral arthritis was independently predicted by female gender (AOR=2.137, 95% CI 1.117-4.085, p=0.022) and presenting symptoms (AOR=0.057, 95% CI 0.023-0.142, p<0.001). PsA in this Saudi cohort is characterized by early onset, balanced gender distribution, a high metabolic comorbidity burden, and conservative biologic use. Presenting symptoms were the strongest independent predictors of both arthritis phenotypes, while female gender predicted peripheral involvement, providing region-specific insights for tailored management.

items.title: Comparison between Janus kinase inhibitor monotherapy and combination therapy with methotrexate in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: insight from the National Database of Rheumatic Diseases in Japan (NinJa) registry.
items.abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are effective for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and can be used as monotherapy; however, the clinical benefit of concomitant methotrexate (MTX) and the optimal MTX dose in JAKi-treated patients remain unclear in real-world settings. In this study, we aimed to clarify the roles of MTX by comparing the patient profiles between JAKi monotherapy (Mono) and combination with MTX (Combi) using the National Database of Rheumatic Diseases in Japan (NinJa). Using the 2022 version of the NinJa database, we analyzed RA patients treated with JAKi. Patients were classified into Mono and Combi groups. Clinical characteristics, disease activity, remission rates, and hospitalization due to serious adverse events (SAEs) were compared. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score (PS)-matched analyses were performed to adjust for confounding factors. Associations between MTX dose and disease activity were examined using correlation and multiple regression analyses. Among the enrolled patients (n = 1315), 544 (41.3%) received Combi therapy. Patients in the Combi group were younger, had shorter disease duration, and showed lower DAS28 (ESR) and HAQ scores than those in the Mono group. DAS28 (ESR)-defined remission rate was higher in the Combi group (50.0% vs. 38.1%, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that MTX use was independently associated with DAS28 (ESR)-defined remission (odds ratio [OR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-2.04). In PS-matched analyses, Combi therapy remained associated with lower DAS28 (ESR) values and higher remission rates. MTX dose was not associated with disease activity among patients receiving Combi therapy. Hospitalization due to SAEs occurred in 11.0% of JAKi-treated patients and was not independently associated with MTX use, whereas glucocorticoid use was a significant risk factor for several SAEs. In real-world clinical practice, Combi therapy with JAKi and MTX was associated with higher remission rates without increasing the risk of SAEs. However, MTX dose did not influence disease activity, suggesting that low-dose MTX may be sufficient when used in combination with JAKi. Although further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term outcomes, Combi therapy was associated with lower DAS28(ESR)-defined disease activity and without observing a clear association with an increase in SAEs in this cross-sectional real-world analysis.

items.title: Absent fluorodeoxyglucose uptake in thoracic aorta and subclavian arteries as a potential indicator for visual impairment in giant cell arteritis: A hypothesis-generating study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the risk of visual impairment in giant cell arteritis (GCA) by integrating the findings of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging with clinical and laboratory parameters. We retrospectively analyzed 54 patients with GCA who underwent PET/CT. We evaluated the association between visual impairment and clinical characteristics, including C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and the anatomical distribution of vascular lesions on PET/CT (e.g., proximal large-vessel [LV] uptake). Furthermore, an unsupervised hierarchical cluster analysis was performed based on FDG uptake patterns. The absence of FDG uptake in the thoracic aorta and subclavian arteries (LV uptake (-)) was associated with visual impairment. In patients presenting with cranial symptoms, the combination of LV uptake (-) and low CRP levels identified a subgroup at a high risk for visual impairment (incidence: 90.0%, odds ratio: 49.1). Furthermore, the cluster analysis identified a subgroup (Cluster 1: upper and lower limb pattern) that shares the low-inflammatory characteristic of this clinical profile. The absence of systemic large-vessel lesions on PET/CT may be associated with an increased risk of visual impairment in GCA. This clinical profile lacking systemic inflammation (LV uptake (-) and low CRP) may be clinically important to identify patients at high risk of visual impairment. Key Points • The absence of large-vessel lesions on PET/CT may be associated with an increased risk of visual impairment in GCA. • Combining cranial symptoms, low CRP, and absent large-vessel inflammation may suggest a higher ocular ischemia risk. • Excluding large-vessel vasculitis via PET/CT assists in stratifying these high-risk patients.

items.title: Dermatomyositis as a paraneoplastic entity associated with thyroid cancer: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a rare autoimmune disease that affects both skin and muscle tissue. In some patients, it can serve as a paraneoplastic signal of an underlying malignancy. While its link to lung, ovarian, and gastrointestinal tumours is well recognized, its association with thyroid cancer remains scarcely explored. This review aimed to summarize and analyse the available clinical evidence on the coexistence of DM and thyroid cancer. A systematic search was performed in PubMed and Scopus from January 2000 to September 2025, following PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included clinical reports, case series, and observational analyses that documented a temporal or clinical relationship between both conditions. An exploratory retrospective assessment of the applicability of the 2017 ACR/EULAR criteria was also performed. Nine studies met the inclusion criteria. Most patients were women with an average age of 48 years. Papillary thyroid carcinoma was the most common histological subtype. The classic form of DM was predominant, and Gottron's papules along with the heliotrope rash were the most frequent cutaneous findings. Clinical improvement was commonly observed after treatment of the thyroid malignancy. The serological profile was heterogeneous and incomplete; two patients were anti-Jo-1 positive, one was anti-MDA5 positive, and one was anti-Ro52 positive. These findings reinforce the importance of considering thyroid cancer among the possible paraneoplastic causes of dermatomyositis. Early detection of characteristic cutaneous signs may be key to identifying an underlying tumour at initial stages and improving patient prognosis.

items.title: Clinical interpretation and cutoff scores for manual ability measured by ABILHAND-RA questionnaire in rheumatoid arthritis: A receiver operating characteristic analysis study.
items.abstract: Although the ABILHAND-RA questionnaire demonstrates strong psychometric properties for assessing manual ability in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, cut-off scores have not yet been established, limiting its clinical interpretability and comparability across studies. The purpose of this study was to establish cut-off scores for ABILHAND-RA questionnaire in rheumatoid arthritis. Cross-sectional study. This study included 186 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (84.9% female, mean age 51.91 ± 11.01 years, mean disease duration 8.89 ± 7.57 years). ABILHAND-RA questionnaire, Disease Activity Score 28 (DAS28), grip strength, Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and Disabilities of Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) were evaluated. Optimal cut-off scores for ABILHAND-RA were determined using receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, and specificity analyses. Patients were 84.9% female, mean age 51.9±11.0 years, with a mean disease duration 8.9±7.6 years). Due to extreme sample homogeneity (99.2% of patients with reduced grip strength), a severe ceiling/floor effect precluded its use as a clinical anchor. Consequently, optimal ABILHAND-RA cut-off points were determined based on HAQ, DASH, and DAS28 anchors. The ABILHAND-RA cut-off logits were 1.9 for HAQ; 1.8 and 1.5 for DASH; and 1.6, 1.6, and 1.5 for DAS28. Correspondingly, the raw scores were 43.5 for HAQ; 43.5 and 42.5 for DASH; and 34.5, 41.5, and 28.5 for DAS28. All estimated area under the curve (AUC) values were significant, indicating discriminatory performance better than chance. In particular, the thresholds calibrated against HAQ and DASH demonstrated good accuracy with AUC values above 0.80. The highest determined by the AUC was observed for the cut-off based on HAQ (AUC 0.89, 95%CI: 0.82-0.96). The ABILHAND-RA cut-off value of 1.914 logits is recommended, as the HAQ-based cut-off demonstrated the highest overall discriminatory accuracy.

items.title: Lupus Nephritis in Pregnancy: A Case-Based Approach to Diagnosis and Management.
items.abstract: Pregnancy presents both a unique opportunity to diagnose previously unrecognized lupus nephritis (LN) and a critical period that influences long-term renal and maternal outcomes in women with established disease. For many young women, pregnancy represents their first significant interaction with the healthcare system. Abnormal findings such as persistent hematuria or proteinuria should not be dismissed as physiologic changes of pregnancy; rather, they should prompt appropriate evaluation for underlying kidney disease. In selected cases, kidney biopsy remains an important diagnostic tool during pregnancy when the results are expected to alter management. In women with established LN, disease activity at conception is the strongest modifiable predictor of maternal and fetal outcomes. Consequently, pregnancy should ideally be planned during sustained disease quiescence, underscoring the importance of preconception counseling, avoidance of unplanned pregnancies, and optimization of pregnancy-compatible immunosuppressive therapy. Pregnancy in women with LN poses several unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, including risk stratification, medication adjustments, prevention of disease flares, and management of maternal and fetal complications. A major clinical challenge is differentiating an LN flare from preeclampsia, as both conditions share overlapping clinical and laboratory features but require fundamentally different management strategies. Advances in angiogenic biomarkers, fetal surveillance, and multidisciplinary care have improved the ability to distinguish these conditions and optimize outcomes. Using a real clinical case scenario, this review discusses current evidence on the diagnosis and management of LN before and during pregnancy, including preconception counseling, disease monitoring, therapeutic considerations, and maternal and fetal risk assessment, emphasizing the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary care.

items.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
items.abstract: Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging. This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers. 161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment. In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

items.title: Incidence and prevalence of adult-onset Still's disease in South Korea: a 20-year nationwide population-based study.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disorder with limited population-based epidemiological data. We estimated the nationwide incidence and prevalence of AOSD in South Korea and assessed temporal trends. As a secondary exploratory aim, we also examined claims-based treatment trajectories. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data from 2002 to 2022. Annual incidence and prevalence were age- and sex-standardised to the 2019 Korean population. Temporal trends were evaluated using log-linear regression and one-joinpoint analyses. Patients were additionally grouped according to claims-based medication trajectories. Among 15,000 individuals with an AOSD diagnostic code, 4,825 met the case definition; 4,600 incident cases diagnosed during 2003-2022 were included. Age- and sex-adjusted annual incidence remained below 1 per 100,000 population (0.28-0.75), with no significant overall temporal change (annual percent change [APC], 1.41%; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.58 to 3.44; p = 0.155). Age- and sex-adjusted prevalence increased from 0.91 per 100,000 in 2003 to 10.02 per 100,000 in 2022 (APC, 12.51%; 95% CI, 10.56 to 14.50; p < 0.001). Across successive 5-year periods, the proportion of female patients decreased from 72.9% to 66.1%, whereas mean age at diagnosis increased from 41.7 to 47.5 years. Under prespecified operational rules, 3.0% of patients were grouped as monocyclic, 39.6% as polycyclic, 17.7% as chronic, and 39.6% as unclassified. AOSD in South Korea is rare, with low overall incidence but steadily increasing prevalence. Exploratory treatment trajectory analyses may complement population-level epidemiological assessment.

items.title: Peripheral blood CD99hiPD-1+ T-cell expansion distinguishes early systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: To investigate CD99- and programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1)-associated T-cell subsets in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and evaluate their clinical relevance and diagnostic potential for early disease detection. Peripheral blood samples were obtained from 37 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve patients with SLE and 33 healthy controls, and 24 patients with pSS as a disease-control group. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated and analyzed by flow cytometry using antibodies against CD3, CD4, CD8, CD99, PD-1, CCR7, and CD45RA to characterize CD99- and PD-1-defined T-cell subsets and differentiation states. Correlations between T-cell subsets and clinical indicators were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed to evaluate diagnostic performance for early SLE detection. Circulating T cells from early SLE patients showed preferential co-expression of CD99 and PD-1, with significantly higher PD-1 levels in CD99hi than in CD99int T cells. CD99hiPD-1+ cells were enriched in effector memory compartments and were least frequent in naïve T cells.Patients with SLE exhibited a broad expansion of CD99hiPD-1+ T cells across multiple CD4+ and CD8+ differentiation states. CD99/PD-1-defined subsets correlated with serological indicators of disease activity, including autoantibodies and complement consumption. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance of individual subsets (area under the curve [AUC] 0.54-0.78), whereas a multivariable logistic model integrating 12 subsets improved discrimination for early SLE (AUC 0.867). CD99hiPD-1+ T cells are expanded across multiple T-cell subsets in SLE and correlate with serological indicators of disease activity, suggesting potential value as immunological markers for early diagnosis.

items.title: FcRn beyond IgG recycling in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in which autoantibody titers alone do not account for disease activity, the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) links their persistence in the circulation to the routing of immune complexes (ICs) and antigen presentation. The recycling of monomeric IgG maintains the pool available to form these complexes, whereas their multivalency engages FcRn in pathways that direct their degradation and the presentation of their autoantigens. It is not the functions themselves, but the cell type in which they operate, that shapes their consequences. This cell dependence results in distinct effects, from the placental transfer of anti-SSA/Ro antibodies to renal clearance or inflammatory functions. Extracellular signals and intracellular mechanisms can locally modulate FcRn expression. Early therapeutic data provide clinical proof of concept in SLE, but the inhibitors evaluated primarily target IgG recycling and transport, without directly elucidating the intracellular handling of ICs. Linking local FcRn expression to IC fate should clarify its contribution to lupus manifestations and the scope of its therapeutic blockade.

items.title: FAIR-Lupus: A Descriptive Monte Carlo Exploration of Excess-Risk Scores in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: BackgroundFAIR-Lupus explores the Normalized Excess-Risk Contribution (NERC), a descriptive mathematical index comparing selected prevalence-weighted association scores in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). It does not estimate causal attribution or attributable disease fractions.MethodsA newly specified analysis replaced the submitted results. Two fixed synthetic cohorts of 100,000 subjects represented female SLE susceptibility and established SLE. We propagated multiplier uncertainty through 10,000 Monte Carlo draws and examined determinant exclusions, correlations preserving exposure frequencies, an illustrative interaction, and EBV prevalence scenarios. All exposure prevalences and the four flare risk multipliers were illustrative. No observed outcomes were analysed.ResultsIncident-scenario median NERC was 50.3% for family history and 34.7% for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) seropositivity; their rank-one frequencies were 75.31% and 24.66%. Flare-scenario medians were 35.6% for stress, 26.7% for respiratory infection, 21.5% for occupational ultraviolet exposure, and 14.8% for PM 2 . 5 . Excluding family history increased EBV median NERC to 70.8%. Correlation alone produced no change when marginal exposure counts were fixed. Varying EBV prevalence from 70% to 98% changed its median share from 28.1% to 35.4%.ConclusionsNERC percentages depend on the selected determinants, exposure prevalences and multipliers; they are not proportions of disease attributable to those determinants. FAIR-Lupus is a methodological exploration without empirical validation and cannot support clinical, occupational-health or individualized causal decisions.

items.title: National statement of clinical and therapeutic approach of patients with systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease in Belgium on behalf of the Flemish network on rare connective tissue diseases.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by multi-organ involvement and a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality. Following the recent national adoption of the European Reference Network on Rare and Complex Connective Tissue and Musculoskeletal Diseases (ReCONNET) SSc patient pathways by the Flemish Network on Rare Connective Tissue Diseases, this statement aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the clinical and therapeutic management of systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) within the Belgian healthcare setting. A multidisciplinary panel of Belgian experts in interstitial lung disease and systemic sclerosis, together with patient representatives, reviewed current evidence and international recommendations. The panel developed consensus-based guidance adapted to the Belgian context, taking into account clinical practice, healthcare organization and treatment accessibility. The expert panel consolidated key recommendations for the diagnosis, monitoring, multidisciplinary management and treatment of SSc-ILD. Particular emphasis was placed on addressing the complexities of disease management and the high morbidity and mortality associated with SSc-ILD, while ensuring applicability within the Belgian healthcare system. Despite the availability of international guidelines for SSc-ILD, differences in therapeutic access, reimbursement policies and the organization of multidisciplinary care necessitate country-specific guidance. This Belgian expert statement aims to support harmonized, equitable and timely access to optimal care for patients with SSc-ILD.

items.title: Clinical Frequency and Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: The occurrence of peripheral neuropathy (PN) in dermatomyositis (DM) is poorly characterized. To characterize the occurrence, clinical patterns, and electrophysiological features of PN in patients with DM. This cohort study used data from a single academic center database of patients with DM who were enrolled between July 2008 and December 2025. Patients with PN were identified through medical record review of problem lists, encounter diagnoses, and clinical notes. PN diagnosis was established by clinical examination, nerve conduction study (NCS), or skin punch biopsy. Patients with PN that was associated with diabetes or prediabetes, vitamin deficiency, infection, trauma, nerve compression, radiculopathy, or neurotoxic medication were excluded. DM subtype, autoantibody positivity, and systemic manifestations. Main outcomes were frequency and clinical/electrophysiological characteristics of PN among patients with DM. Among 640 patients with DM (median [IQR] age, 60 [40.8-70.0] years; 546 [85.3%] female; 94 [14.7%] male), 120 (18.8%) had clinically documented PN (median [IQR] age, 60 [50.5-70.8] years; 104 [86.7%] female; 16 [13.3%] male), ascertained at a median (IQR) of 3 (1-9) years after DM diagnosis. Patients with PN were significantly more likely to have classic DM than patients without PN (75 of 120 [62.5%] vs 269 of 520 [51.7%]; P = .03). Patients with PN had higher rates of arthralgia (95 of 120 [79.2%] vs 93 of 511 [18.2%]; P < .001) and Raynaud syndrome (67 of 120 [55.8%] vs 198 of 511 [38.7%]; P < .001), and lower myositis-specific antibody positivity (28 of 104 patients [26.9%] vs 112 of 295 [38.0%]; P = .04), than patients without PN. NCS was performed in 61 patients, with positive findings in 39 patients (63.9%) and negative findings in 22 patients (36.1%). Mixed sensory-motor polyneuropathy was most common (23 of 39 patients [58.9%]), followed by pure sensory neuropathy (12 of 39 patients [30.8%]), with axonal features predominating (37 of 39 patients [94.9%]) over demyelinating features (2 of 39 patients [5.1%]). Small-fiber neuropathy was biopsy-confirmed in 4 patients (3.3%) and clinically suspected without biopsy confirmation in 16 patients (13.3%). In this cohort study, clinically documented PN was identified in nearly one-fifth of the DM cohort after exclusion of secondary causes and was associated with classic DM subtype and higher rates of arthralgia and Raynaud syndrome. The predominance of axonal over demyelinating patterns on NCS suggests inflammatory axonal injury as one possible mechanism, though other causes cannot be excluded. These findings suggest PN is an underrecognized systemic association of DM warranting heightened clinical awareness and further mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Low Disease Activity and Drug-Free Remission in Anti-MDA5 Dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5)-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5-DM) is associated with rapid progression and high early mortality, but long-term outcomes beyond the early high-risk phase remain poorly characterized. To evaluate the attainability, associated factors, and durability of low disease activity (LDA) and drug-free remission (DFR) in patients with MDA5-DM. This retrospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center in China included consecutive patients with MDA5-DM who were enrolled between August 2003 and July 2023 and followed up through August 2025. Median follow-up was 5.7 (IQR, 3.4-7.4) years. The data were analyzed from September 2025 through December 2025. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics. Primary outcomes were experiencing LDA and DFR. Secondary outcomes included relapse after LDA or DFR and patient-reported outcomes assessed using the Patient Global Assessment and Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index. Of 561 screened patients, 523 (93.2%) were included. Among 523 patients with MDA5-DM, 345 (65.9%) were female, 178 (34.1%) were male, and the median age at disease onset was 50.0 years (IQR, 41.0-57.5 years). Interstitial lung disease was present in 488 patients (93.3%) at baseline. Cumulative 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year all-cause mortality was 28.1%, 30.5%, 30.8%, and 31.7%, respectively. The 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year cumulative incidences of LDA were 3.1%, 47.1%, 59.0%, and 66.8%, respectively; corresponding incidences of DFR were 0%, 5.0%, 15.1%, and 31.0%, respectively. The median time from enrollment was 23 months (IQR, 18-34) for LDA and 46 months (IQR, 37-67) for DFR. Respiratory failure was associated with lower rates of LDA (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 0.31; 95% CI, 0.19-0.51) and DFR (sHR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87), whereas a higher CD8-positive T-cell count was associated with higher rates of LDA (sHR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.08-1.22) and DFR (sHR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.09-1.31). The 5-year relapse-free probabilities were 76.7% after LDA and 82.0% after DFR. LDA and DFR were associated with lower Patient Global Assessment and Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index scores compared with non-LDA or non-DFR states. The findings of this cohort study suggest that LDA was an attainable and durable long-term outcome for many patients with MDA5-DM, whereas DFR occurred less frequently. These findings may inform long-term disease control targets and treatment expectations in MDA5-DM.

items.title: Therapeutic values of medicinal plants on inflammation indexes and the severity of pain in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disorder that is described as inflammation in the synovial tissues of joints, cartilages, bones, and less frequently in extra-articular localities, which affects the quality of life, especially in older population. Various medicinal plants and their bioactive compounds have demonstrated significant anti-inflammatory effects by modulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, as well as inhibiting NF-κB signaling pathways in rheumatoid arthritis. This review aimed to study the therapeutic values of some medicinal plants on inflammatory indexes in RA patients. All electronic databases were searched for articles on November 2025 by searching "medicinal plant," and "Rheumatoid arthritis" as the key terms. After collecting the relevant documents, the data were extracted and described. In total, data of 43 articles with 7523 included patients were extracted. Findings demonstrated that some medicinal plants are rich sources of active constituents, which can affect inflammatory factors such as levels of serum rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated protein antibodies, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, that subsequently leads to improvement of visual analogue scale, disease activity score with 28-joint counts, health assessment questionnaire, joint count for pain. Medicinal plants and herbal formulations are promising sources to replace or at least limit the excessive consumption of NSAIDs in RA diseases and associated comorbidities. Accordingly, appropriate herbal therapy may be helpful in treating the RA or minimizing the RA-associated symptoms.

items.title: Multimodal ultrasound in assessing disease activity in axial spondyloarthritis: correlation and evaluation value.
items.abstract: To investigate the correlation between multimodal ultrasound parameters and disease activity in radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA). A total of 146 patients with r-axSpA and nr-axSpA were enrolled. Disease activity was assessed using the ASDAS-CRP index. Patients with ASDAS-CRP < 2.1 were classified as the remission group (n = 94), and those with ASDAS-CRP ≥ 2.1 as the active disease group (n = 52). All patients underwent multimodal ultrasound examination, including Power Doppler ultrasound (PDU) of the sacroiliac joint (SIJ), the Glasgow Ultrasound Enthesitis Scoring System (GUESS), and strain elastography (SE). Discriminative performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis. The active disease group showed significantly higher SIJ blood flow grades, higher GUESS scores at all entheseal sites, and lower elasticity scores indicating softer tendon tissue during active disease (all P < 0.05). The combined multimodal ultrasound score achieved an AUC of 0.921, significantly outperforming the individual blood flow score (AUC = 0.755), GUESS score (AUC = 0.571), and elasticity score (AUC = 0.569) (all P < 0.05). Multimodal ultrasound parameters are significantly correlated with axSpA disease activity. A composite multimodal ultrasound score integrating PDU, GUESS, and SE markedly enhances evaluative accuracy, providing an objective and comprehensive imaging basis for clinical decision-making.

items.title: Beyond inflammation: Peripheral neuropathy, neuropathic pain, and central sensitization in ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease in which pain may result from inflammatory, neuropathic, and central sensitization mechanisms. This study aimed to determine the frequency of peripheral neuropathy, neuropathic pain, and central sensitization in AS patients and evaluate their associations with disease activity, quality of life, functional impairment, and electrophysiological findings. This cross-sectional study included 45 patients fulfilling the modified New York criteria for AS. Peripheral neuropathy, neuropathic pain, and central sensitization were assessed using standard nerve conduction studies, PainDETECT, and the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI), respectively. Disease activity, enthesitis, functional impairment, and quality of life were evaluated using validated instruments. Associations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation, and independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Peripheral neuropathy was identified in (48.9%) of patients, with affected patients being significantly older than those without neuropathy. Central sensitization (CSI ≥ 40) was present in 16/45 patients (35.6%). CSI scores showed significant positive correlations with disease activity, functional impairment, and enthesitis scores. PainDETECT scores correlated significantly with disease activity indices and functional impairment. Age was the only independent predictor of peripheral neuropathy (OR 1.109, 95% CI 1.02-1.21). Peripheral neuropathy, neuropathic pain, and central sensitization are common in AS and are associated with higher disease activity, more functional impairment, and poor quality of life. Increasing age independently predicts peripheral neuropathy. These findings support incorporating neurological and pain-processing assessments into the routine evaluation of AS and warrant longitudinal studies to explore causality and therapeutic implications. Key Points • Pain in ankylosing spondylitis extends beyond inflammatory mechanisms. • Central sensitization and neuropathic pain are associated with disease activity and functional impairment. • Peripheral neuropathy is frequently detected, although increasing age is its only independent predictor.

items.title: Severe Fetal Anemia and Pancytopenia in Maternal Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Treated with Serial Intrauterine Transfusions and Intravenous Immunoglobulin: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Severe fetal anemia with hydrops and multilineage cytopenia is rarely reported in pregnancies complicated by maternal systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We report a 33-year-old woman with SLE and maternal thrombocytopenia whose fetus developed hydrops and an MCA-PSV of 1.823 MoM at 24+6 weeks. Fetal sampling before the first intrauterine transfusion (IUT) showed hemoglobin 3.3 g/dL, hematocrit 10.5%, WBC 0.28 × 10³/µL and platelets 17 × 10³/µL. The first IUT at 25+6 weeks corrected the anemia, although profound leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were documented immediately afterward. Repeat sampling immediately before a second IUT at 28+1 weeks showed hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 0.14 × 10³/µL and platelets 26 × 10³/µL. Serial IUTs corrected fetal anemia; maternal IVIG was given empirically because of concern for an additional immune contribution, without proof of immune-mediated cell destruction or an independent IVIG effect. Fetal growth restriction and abnormal Dopplers contributed to delivery at 33+6 weeks. The neonate had normal blood counts without postnatal transfusion. This case highlights the importance of targeted evaluation for fetal anemia when concerning sonographic findings arise in SLE pregnancies.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of the Effectiveness of Methotrexate Co-Administration with Baricitinib in Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment.
items.abstract: To evaluate the effect of methotrexate (MTX) co-administration with baricitinib (BAR) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment using a multicenter registry. A total of 296 patients with RA treated with BAR were included (167 with MTX and 129 without MTX). Treatment effectiveness over 52 weeks was evaluated using propensity score-based overlap weighting to adjust for baseline differences. Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was applied to identify distinct longitudinal response patterns. After overlap weighting, baseline characteristics were successfully balanced between groups (standardized mean differences <0.1). No significant differences were observed between the -MTX and +MTX groups in treatment retention (76.3% vs. 83.7%, p=0.213), CDAI scores at week 52 (5.7 [95% CI 4.2-7.1] vs. 5.8 [95% CI 4.5-7.1], p=0.90), or remission rates (32.1% vs. 34.5%, p=0.70). GBTM identified four distinct trajectories of disease activity; however, the distribution of MTX use did not differ across trajectory groups. After adjustment for baseline differences, MTX co-administration was not associated with improved clinical outcomes or response trajectories during BAR therapy. These findings may inform treatment decisions for patients unable to receive concomitant MTX.

items.title: Metabolomic signatures in synovial tissue characterize osteoarthritis-like phenotypes in rheumatoid arthritis of knee.
items.abstract: Osteoarthritis-like rheumatoid arthritis (OA-like RA) is a clinical phenotype characterized by suppressed joint destruction and radiographic features mimicking OA, despite an underlying RA diagnosis. This study aimed to elucidate the pathophysiological distinctions among OA-like RA, typical RA, and OA through histopathological and metabolomic profiling of synovial tissues. Twenty-four patients with RA and six with OA undergoing total knee arthroplasty were enrolled. RA cases were classified into two subgroups: OA-like RA (n = 10; predominant osteoarthritic changes) and typical RA (n = 14; classic RA findings). Knee synovial tissues harvested intraoperatively were evaluated using the Krenn score and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS)-based metabolomics. Among 475 GC-MS-detectable compounds, 211 metabolites were identified. Although statistical significance was attenuated following false discovery rate correction, nominal p-values identified five candidate metabolites with differential abundance: hydroxyproline (a marker of cartilage degradation) and four energy- and inflammation-related metabolites (sucrose, 2-aminoadipic acid, lactic acid, and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid). While the Krenn synovitis score was numerically higher in the typical RA group, there were no statistically significant differences among the groups. This exploratory study provides preliminary metabolomic insights into OA-like RA, warranting larger cohorts to validate these biomarkers and delineate its pathophysiology.

items.title: Distribution Analysis of Foot Ulcers and Gangrene in Japanese Patients With Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Skin ulcers and gangrene are severe complications of systemic sclerosis. Although previous studies have focused on their anatomical distribution on the hands, the precise localization of foot lesions related to systemic sclerosis has not been investigated in detail. This retrospective study evaluated the distribution of foot ulcers and gangrene and analyzed their association with the season of onset to explore the possible contribution of cold-induced ischemia and external factors, including mechanical stress. We included 25 patients with a mean age of 73.2 ± 12.8 years. The locations of 44 foot ulcer lesions and 12 gangrene onset events were mapped using a standardized foot template. Foot ulcers were classified as apical, periungual, or other ulcers, and the season of onset was categorized as the cold season, from October to March, or the non-cold season, from April to September. Five patients had both foot ulcers and gangrene, and only two patients presented with both simultaneously. Gangrene onset events during the cold season were more frequently associated with multiple-toe involvement than those during the non-cold season (p = 0.045). Among foot ulcers, apical lesions were observed exclusively during the cold season and were significantly associated with cold-season onset (p = 0.032). In contrast, periungual and other ulcers occurred in both predefined seasons. These findings suggest that cold-season ischemic factors may contribute to gangrene and apical foot ulcers, whereas external stimuli, including mechanical stress, may be involved in non-apical foot ulcers. Further prospective studies incorporating objective vascular assessments and direct evaluation of mechanical factors are warranted.
